title: Rheumatic Heart Disease: Secondary Prophylaxis and Specialist Follow-Up

evidenceAudit.scope: Children and adults with acute rheumatic fever (ARF) or rheumatic heart disease (RHD) in primary care and cardiology clinics: diagnosis basics, benzathine benzylpenicillin G (BPG) secondary prophylaxis with interval, oral and penicillin-allergy alternatives, duration by severity, echocardiography follow-up, endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures and pre-pregnancy counselling. Uses an Australian Prescriber review based on the Australian RHD guideline, the WHO 2024 guideline summary and product information. Acute heart failure from carditis and valve surgery are referred.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi RHD guideline was found; the main source is Australian and a review, not the full guideline.
The full WHO 2024 guideline could not be opened; only its summary page was read.
The phenoxymethylpenicillin and erythromycin product information give adult prophylaxis dosing (penicillin V) or none (erythromycin); child doses for the oral options are not listed.
Duration rules are summarised from the review's Table 2 and should be checked against the full Australian guideline.
Typical normal values for C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and PR interval are not from these sources.

pathophysiology.summary: ARF is an autoimmune reaction days to months after group A streptococcal infection, mainly in immature immune systems (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Pathogenesis). Repeated ARF episodes damage heart valves and cause RHD (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Introduction). Regular BPG prevents new streptococcal infections and recurrences; better adherence improves outcomes (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Secondary prophylaxis). WHO 2024 covers primary prevention, secondary prophylaxis with adherence support and screening for early RHD (WHO 2024, Section Overview).

symptoms: Fever with joint pain, often migratory polyarthritis of large joints (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Clinical features).
Involuntary movements of Sydenham chorea (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Clinical features).
Breathlessness or reduced exercise tolerance in valve disease (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 1 heart failure row).
physicalSigns: New heart murmur from valve disease (carditis) (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Clinical features).
First-degree heart block on electrocardiogram (ECG) (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Investigations).
Erythema marginatum and subcutaneous nodules, rare (under 1%) (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Clinical features).
redFlags: Heart failure from severe acute carditis: specialist cardiology advice (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 1).
Breakthrough ARF despite full adherence: shorten BPG interval to 21 days (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2 footnote).
Severe RHD or previous valve surgery: 21-day interval and long-term or lifelong prophylaxis (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
Pregnancy or planned pregnancy with RHD: pre-conception counselling and specialist care (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Pregnancy).
precipitants: Group A streptococcal throat or skin infection (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Pathogenesis; WHO 2024, Section Overview).
Missed BPG injections (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Secondary prophylaxis).
Childhood and adolescence (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Pathogenesis).

differentials.condition: Other causes of arthritis and fever
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: ARF has no single test; diagnosis uses the Jones criteria (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Diagnosis).

Sydenham chorea follows streptococcal infection (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Clinical features).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Rheumatic mitral or aortic regurgitation or stenosis
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Central to diagnosis and follow-up; mild RHD at 1, 3 and 5 years, moderate every 12 months, severe every 6 months (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Investigations and Table 2).
ruleIn.normalValue: Normal valve leaflets without regurgitation or stenosis

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm diagnosis and severity
actions: Diagnose ARF with the Jones criteria and do echocardiography and ECG (Aust Prescr 2022, Sections Diagnosis and Investigations).
Grade RHD as borderline, mild, moderate or severe to set prophylaxis duration and review frequency (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).

clinicalManagement.title: Eradicate streptococcus at ARF diagnosis
actions: Give a single BPG dose: 1,200,000 units (600,000 units under 20 kg) (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 1).
Treat arthritis with naproxen or ibuprofen and refer severe carditis or chorea to specialists (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 1).

clinicalManagement.title: Start and keep up secondary prophylaxis
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Every 28 days (21 days in selected groups)
actions: Give BPG by deep intramuscular injection (see Medicines) (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2; Bicillin L-A data sheet, Section 4.2).
Use the 21-day interval for breakthrough ARF despite full adherence, severe RHD or after valve surgery (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2 footnote).
Recall from day 21 to keep injections within 28 days (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
Lidocaine is no longer contraindicated with BPG injections (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Secondary prophylaxis).

clinicalManagement.title: Echocardiography follow-up
actions: Borderline: review and echocardiogram at 1 to 2 years; mild: at 1, 3 and 5 years; moderate: every 12 months; severe: every 6 months (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).

clinicalManagement.title: Endocarditis prophylaxis and pregnancy
actions: For certain dental procedures, amoxicillin 2 g (children 50 mg/kg up to 2 g) 60 minutes before; clindamycin if penicillin allergy or recent beta-lactam course (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 3).
Offer pre-conception counselling and specialist care to women with RHD (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Pregnancy).

regimens.indication: Secondary prophylaxis of ARF and RHD
regimens.patientGroup: Adults and children with ARF or RHD
regimens.genericName: Benzathine benzylpenicillin G 1,200,000 units/2.3 mL injection
regimens.dose: 1,200,000 units for 20 kg or more; PAEDIATRIC under 20 kg: 600,000 units (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2; Bicillin L-A data sheet, Section 4.2).
regimens.route: Deep intramuscular injection into the upper outer buttock; never intravenous
regimens.frequency: Every 28 days; every 21 days in high-risk groups
regimens.duration: By severity: see criteria (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2)
adjustments: Excreted by the kidney; consider renal function, especially in older patients (Bicillin L-A data sheet, Section 4.4).
Under 10 kg: 600,000 units is still generally used; seek paediatric advice (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Date of each injection and adherence (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
Observe for anaphylaxis after injection (Bicillin L-A data sheet, Section 4.4).
contraindications: Previous major allergy or anaphylaxis to a penicillin or cephalosporin (Bicillin L-A data sheet, Section 4.3).
Aspirate before injecting; inadvertent intravascular injection causes serious injury (Bicillin L-A data sheet, Sections 4.2 and 4.4).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Jones criteria; no single diagnostic test (Aust Prescr 2022, Section Diagnosis).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Prophylaxis duration, probable or definite ARF without cardiac involvement
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: At least 5 years after the last episode or until age 21, whichever is longer (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
At least 10 years after the last ARF or until age 21 (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
At least 10 years after the last ARF or until age 35 (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Prophylaxis duration, severe RHD or valve surgery
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: At least 10 years after the last ARF or until age 40; often lifelong if surgery is needed (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).

teaching.scope: Children and adults with acute rheumatic fever (ARF) or rheumatic heart disease (RHD) in primary care and cardiology clinics: diagnosis basics, benzathine benzylpenicillin G (BPG) secondary prophylaxis with interval, oral and penicillin-allergy alternatives, duration by severity, echocardiography follow-up, endocarditis prophylaxis for dental procedures and pre-pregnancy counselling. Uses an Australian Prescriber review based on the Australian RHD guideline, the WHO 2024 guideline summary and product information. Acute heart failure from carditis and valve surgery are referred.
learningObjectives: Start BPG secondary prophylaxis after ARF or RHD diagnosis.
Set duration and review frequency by RHD severity.
Use the oral or penicillin-allergy options correctly.
Arrange dental endocarditis prophylaxis and pregnancy counselling.
pitfalls: Stopping prophylaxis too early in moderate or severe RHD.
keyPoints: BPG every 28 days is the standard; 21 days for high-risk groups.
Adherence is the main driver of outcome.

patientEducation: Regular penicillin injections stop new rheumatic fever attacks that damage the heart valves.
Keep every injection appointment; never let a dose run late.
Tell your dentist and obstetrician that you have RHD.
lifestyleAndDiet: Good dental hygiene and regular dental checks.
Seek treatment early for sore throats and skin sores.
mdtReferrals: Primary care; cardiologist; paediatrician; dentist; obstetrician for pregnancy; nursing staff running the injection recall register.
dischargeCriteria: BPG started, injection schedule and recall set up, echocardiography follow-up booked, allergy status recorded.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Injections every 28 days (or 21 days); echocardiography by severity: borderline at 1 to 2 years, mild at 1, 3 and 5 years, moderate yearly, severe every 6 months (Aust Prescr 2022, Table 2).
